## What is implemented

`Observer` requires explicit enablement and exactly a `FakeQueue`. Boolean
`real_client_adapter` requests still fail closed. Passing extracted function
bodies instruments `ClientBarrier.pause/retain/drain/exporter_identity` against
the pinned source and still raises. Queue allocation owns a private synthetic plane;
the caller cannot pass an unrelated byte array to snapshot. A completed writer
record binds run, context generation, allocation generation, job, picture and POC.
Pinning blocks release/rewrite. Pause prevents new submissions, while drain waits
for an external fake worker rather than manufacturing completion itself. All
in-flight jobs must finish, including readers of other allocations.

A preallocated 1474560-byte pool holds at most eight 184320-byte snapshots of only
compression and MV ranges. Metadata/views are prepared before pause; hashes happen
after resume/unpin. The synthetic worker rejects copies taking over 20ms and drains
over 2s. Exceptions during pause stop the experiment and release its pin in `finally`;
there is no automatic playback restart. Payload storage is bounded; Python is not
an allocation-free real-time or kernel implementation. One observer worker per queue.

`copy=False` uses the same pin/pause/drain/validate/resume/unpin sequence and pool,
but skips bytes and hashes. That is a synthetic disturbance-control test, not a
hardware noninterference result. Memory-policy labels describe only this model;
even a caller claiming `verified-coherent-noncached` cannot create a real adapter.
